chunks: And Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from Sama'ah who said:

I asked him about a man who broke his fast by eating or drinking in the month of Ramadan, so he said: 'He has broken his fast, and upon him is its making up (qada'), and he is considered fasting [in terms of obligation] but he must make up his fast and his ablution if he did so deliberately.'

His saying (peace be upon him) in this report 'he makes up his ablution' is on the level of recommendation (istihbab), based on the indication of what we mentioned in the Book of Purity. And it is not obligatory upon that to make up the fast, because if we were to follow the apparent meaning of the report, we would say that making up the purity is also obligatory. But we referred it to recommendation due to the evidence we presented earlier, and that evidence is not present in making up the fast, so it remains upon its apparent meaning regarding the obligation of making up the fast for whoever did that deliberately, as opposed to forgetfulness.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on making up ablution if one breaks their fast deliberately in Ramadan?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling through the chain of Sama'ah, clarifying that while deliberate consumption invalidates the fast and necessitates qada', the requirement to repeat ablution is merely recommended (istihbab) rather than obligatory. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly method of reconciling apparent textual contradictions by prioritizing specific evidence over the literal appearance of the hadith.
